blocks.intro: What the skid leaves on paper, and the claim each document proves.

items.d: Strips carbon dioxide ahead of EDI without dosing caustic, where feed alkalinity is high. Adds: its datasheet, a P&ID line and a FAT check.
Two trains at [duplex train shares offered] each: one runs while the other is sanitized. Adds: the second train’s FAT checks and a changeover test.
Circulates when storage is full, so water does not stand in the membranes. Adds: a control sequence, tested at FAT.
After DI or EDI, where microbial margin is needed. Ultraviolet (UV) lowers the viable count; it does not sanitize. Adds: a P&ID line, FAT check.
A concentrate recovery RO stage cuts water to drain where sewer charges or supply limits matter. Adds: revised membrane projections and a FAT check.

blocks.intro: Each tag names what the option adds on paper. Your proposal marks it included or priced, with its lead time effect.

items.q: Our draft URS names stainless steel and hot sanitization. Does PP fit?
items.a: Not as written. Natural polypropylene (PP) is rated 0 to 80 °C, and its pressure rating falls as it heats. If you need a hot loop or stainless product contact, PP is the wrong choice. Otherwise, rewrite those rows in your user requirement specification (URS) as outcomes you can test. Where we still differ, our proposal says where and why.

items.q: How is the PP skid sanitized?
items.a: Skid sanitization: [sanitization method for the PP skid]; heat-sanitizable RO and EDI: [heat-sanitizable RO and EDI, yes or no]. After any chemical sanitization, removal of the sanitant is proven before use (WHO TRS 1033). Routine 80 °C at loop pressure, a hot-held loop or steam needs a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) or stainless loop [whether we quote PVDF].

Single-pass reverse osmosis (RO) with electrodeionization (EDI) suits feed with moderate dissolved solids. Double pass adds margin on conductivity, total organic carbon and silica for high-solids feed.

items.q: Critical water or boiler make-up, not PW: does this skid fit?
items.a: Yes, if your use passes the fit check. For critical water (ANSI/AAMI ST108:2023) or boiler make-up, the RO train is designed to the limit your standard names. Whether DI or EDI is fitted follows that limit: [configurations offered for this use].

items.q: How do you handle cold winter feed?
items.a: We size at your coldest feed, or add a heat exchanger. Rated at 25 °C, reverse osmosis (RO) can lose a third or more of its output at 5 °C.

items.q: Our supply is chloraminated. What changes?
items.a: Pretreatment removes chloramine before the membranes. We design for the ammonia it releases together with CO₂ control.

items.q: How do we know it will pass IQ/OQ?
items.a: Two acceptance tests come first. The factory acceptance test (FAT) proves function before shipping. Your quality unit approves its protocol first and can witness it with [FAT witness notice, working days] notice. The site acceptance test (SAT), then installation and operational qualification (IQ/OQ), prove it on your site and feed water.

items.q: What keeps the water in specification after handover?
items.a: Three things on your side: sanitization on the agreed schedule, daily conductivity and alarm checks, and a kept log. The operating manual sets each one. A service plan adds our visits and calibrations.
